newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SOCCER-SWEDES DESPERATE TO WIN AGAINST IN-FORM SCOTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDES DESPERATE TO WIN AGAINST IN-FORM SCOTS.

text.p: Sweden will rely on their international exports on Wednesday to restore their chances of qualifying for the World Cup finals against in-form Scotland.

Scotland, unbeaten with four wins and two draws in group four, are confident they can beat a Swedish side which has looked lacklustre and uninspired in the last six months, prompting reports coach Tommy Svensson is on his way out.
A Scottish victory would allow the visitors to begin packing their suitcases for next year's World Cup finals in France.

"They're incredibly strong in defence and will be determined to get a draw. One point will be enough for them to get Scotland first place in the group," said Svensson after Tuesday's training session.
Svensson, who broke a long-standing habit by announcing his team in advance of the match, added: "Scotland are also very quick on the break so we have to make sure we don't get caught napping."

On paper, Sweden have an impressive line-up, with players such as Anderlecht's Per Zetterburg, Leicester City's Pontus Kamark and Bologna's Kennet Andersson making up a squad almost exclusively comprising players who earn their salaries outside Sweden.

Kamark, who marked Brazilian star Juninho out of England's League Cup final this month, could be central to Svensson's bid for a victory. He returns to the national side after 18 months away because of injury.

"It's great to be back and meet the guys again. It's almost like coming home," said Kamark, hero of Leicester's 1-0 Cup victory against Middlesborough, when he marked the dazzling Juninho out of two games.

Svensson was putting a brave face on his team's recent dismal performance. "We're really looking forward to this match, Now it's time for us to take revenge for all the knocks we took in the autumn," he said.
"We had a high intensity work-out because the players needed a thorough shake-out," Svensson told reporters, adding his team would be at full strength for the match.
Sweden lost at home to Austria on October 9 and away to Scotland on Nov 10 and are third in the group.
Scotland lead it and a victory here would mean they would finish no worse than second in the group.
Although they lost 2-0 to Sweden in a friendly in October 1995, Scotland have won their last four World Cup matches against the Swedes.

They beat them 1-0 in a qualifier in Stockholm in 1980 and 2-0 at home a year later. Scotland also beat Sweden 2-1 in the World Cup finals in Italy in 1990, and won again in this competition, 1-0 at home in November.
Sweden - Thomas Ravelli; Gary Sundgren, Patrik Andersson, Joachim Bjrklund, Pontus Kamark; Jonas Thern, Per Zetterberg, Stefan Schwarz; Andreas Andersson, Kennet Andersson, Martin Dahlin.
Scotland (probable) - Jim Leighton; Tom Boyd, Craig Burley, Colin Calderwood, Colin Hendry; Tosh McKinlay, Paul Lambert, Gary McAllister; John Collins Kevin Gallacher, Darren Jackson.
